featureRequest:
# Opt-in focus streak (focusSheen prop) (and 1 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
The developer likes the one-time light streak that the split button's chevron plays on mount. They want a similar streak as an opt-in feature on any ZestButton, regular or split. It should play across the whole button when it gets keyboard focus, and the host should also be able to trigger it from code. This helps users see which button has focus on screens with many components.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Opt-in focus streak (focusSheen prop) (confirmed)
Add an opt-in boolean prop (working name `focusSheen`, default off). When on, a light streak sweeps across the whole button when it gets keyboard focus, using `:focus-visible` (not plain `:focus`, so mouse clicks do not trigger it). Direction: starts at the top-right corner and sweeps to the bottom-left at about 45 degrees. This is the assistant's reading of 'about 45 degrees from top right', and the developer was asked to correct it if wrong but did not. Duration about 0.6s, play once per focus arrival. The existing focus ring stays the main focus signal, and the streak is decoration only. Regular button: use a `::after` layer on the button itself. The base `.button` already has position:relative and overflow:hidden, so it clips the streak. Regular buttons use no ::before or ::after today, so there is no clash. Split button: the streak covers the whole control (both segments), not per segment. Put position:relative and overflow:hidden on `.splitButtonContainer` and add a streak layer to it, triggered with `:has(:focus-visible)` (or `:focus-within`) on the wrapper so focus on either segment plays one sweep. The wrapper has no border-radius today, so give it a radius matching the buttons' outer corners so the clip looks right. The dropdown menu will not be clipped, because it renders in a Radix Portal outside the wrapper. When the focus streak is active on a split button, turn off the chevron's own mount streak (`.dropdownTrigger::before`) so two streaks do not play together. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling the streak. Colour: white at about 65% suits solid buttons. It would barely show on outline, text and dashed styles, so decide whether the first version covers only solid styles or adjusts the colour per style.

Evidence:
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:572-586 (existing chevron mount streak, ::before)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:588-600
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:151-153 (.button position:relative, overflow:hidden)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:179-182 (focus ring uses :focus-visible)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:495-498 (.splitButtonContainer inline-flex, no position or overflow)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:653-656 (reduced-motion disables mount streak)
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:418 (regular button uses the shared button class)
- UI/ZestDropdownMenu.tsx:67-68 (chevron trigger uses the shared button class)
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:453-469 (split wrapper)
- UI/ZestDropdownMenu.tsx:85-87 (menu rendered in a Radix Portal)

### 2. Programmatic streak trigger (sheenTrigger prop) (confirmed)
Add a prop (working name `sheenTrigger`, a number or key) so the host can play the streak from code. Each change of its value plays one streak. The first value on mount does NOT play (the assistant's default, which the developer did not contradict). It works independently of `focusSheen`, so it plays even when `focusSheen` is off. It uses the same streak layer and keyframes as the focus streak. On a split button it sweeps the whole control through the wrapper layer. It plays on disabled buttons too (assistant's default, not contradicted). It is still disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, with no override. The developer chose a changing-value prop over a ref handle or a boolean prop. ZestButton has no forwardRef, so adding a ref would be a bigger API change. Replay needs the animation to restart each time. The suggested approach is to re-key the streak layer on the trigger value, or to remove and re-add the class. This has not been tested in this code, so verify that repeated triggers replay after building.

Evidence:
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:170 (plain React.FC, no forwardRef or useImperativeHandle)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:572-586 (existing streak is CSS-only, so there is no replay logic today)

## Not part of this
- A provider-level default for the focus streak in ZestButtonConfigProvider (left out of the first version).
- A ref handle such as ref.current.sheen(), and adding forwardRef to ZestButton.
- Changing the existing mount streak on the chevron, apart from turning it off on split buttons when the new streak is active.
- Triggering the streak on mouse click (plain :focus).

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Direction: the assistant read '45 degrees from top right' as top-right to bottom-left. The developer did not explicitly confirm this.
- Should the first value of sheenTrigger on mount play a streak? The default is no, and the developer did not confirm.
- Should a trigger play on disabled or busy buttons? The default is yes, and the developer did not confirm.
- Does the first version cover only solid button styles, or adjust the streak colour for outline, text and dashed styles with light backgrounds?
- Exact duration (about 0.6s proposed) and the name of the props are working choices, not confirmed.
- Whether replay on repeated sheenTrigger changes works with the chosen re-key approach has not been tested.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: A button can be configured to play the diagonal light-streak effect when it gains focus. The option is off by default and is turned on per button.
  - Done when: With the option off, focusing the button shows no streak.
  - Done when: With the option on, focusing the button plays the streak.
  - Done when: Both a regular button and a split button can have the option turned on.
- **R2**: The streak is a diagonal band at about 45 degrees that starts from the top-right area of the button and sweeps across the whole button, clipped to the button's shape.
  - Done when: The band is visibly diagonal at about 45 degrees and travels from the top-right towards the opposite side.
  - Done when: No part of the streak is visible outside the button's edges.
- **R3**: When a split button has the option enabled, focusing either segment plays one streak that sweeps across the whole split control, not one streak per segment.
  - Done when: Focusing the main action segment of an opted-in split button plays a single streak spanning the full split control, including the chevron segment.
  - Done when: Focusing the chevron segment of an opted-in split button plays a single streak spanning the full split control, including the main action segment.
  - Done when: The streak is not shown as two separate per-segment streaks on the same split control.
- **R4**: A host can start the streak on a button programmatically through a prop whose value change plays one streak, without the button needing to gain focus.
  - Done when: A host can start the streak on a button that is not focused by changing the trigger prop's value.
  - Done when: Every change of the trigger prop's value plays one streak.
  - Done when: The programmatic trigger works whether or not the focus-triggered option is turned on.

<!--devteam-requirements:-->

sliceReports.summary: Revision 1 slice 1: added the optional boolean `focusSheen` field to ZestCustomProps (off by default, no new export or plumbing) and the CSS focus streak in the shared stylesheet. A regular opted-in button gets one `::after` band clipped by its existing rounded overflow; an opted-in split control gets one whole-control overlay on the split wrapper, keyed to :has(:focus-visible), clipped by its own radius so neither segment's focus ring is cut, and with the chevron mount streak suppressed for that control. The band is a 45-degree gradient travelling top-right to bottom-left over 0.6s, uses currentColor on regular buttons and style+variant+forced-theme markers on split controls, ends transparent, keeps the label above it, and is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Wrote focused behavioural and characterisation tests, and documented the option in documentation/api.md, documentation/features.md, documentation/examples.md and the new docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md. README.md and documentation/configuration.md are left for the other slice as instructed. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build and the full npm test suite (26 suites, 331 tests, all passing).

findings.description: The single white/65% band does not meet R4's 3:1 contrast acceptance for solid buttons in dark theme (worst: dark solid success ~1.5:1), so the feature silently does nothing on those buttons. The new tests only regex-match the CSS source text, so they do not catch this.
findings.evidence: The regular band is `currentColor` (white for every `.solid` button) at peak opacity 0.65 (line 672); the split overlay hardcodes `--zest-focus-sheen-color: #ffffff` (line 692) at the same 0.65 (line 730). Under `.force-dark` / prefers-color-scheme dark, `.solid.success` uses `--zest-color-success-bg: #34d399` (line 110 and line 52), so even fully opaque white is only ~1.92:1 and the 0.65 composite is ~1.51:1; dark solid standard (#3b82f6) and danger (#ef4444) composites are only ~2.42:1 and ~2.35:1, and light success (#059669) ~2.43:1. R4 requires every style/variant/theme to show a band distinguishable from its own background at >=3:1 at the brightest point. On a dark-theme solid success button the white sheen is effectively invisible.
findings.note: Ruled by the arbiter: REV-1 describes the pre-round-2 stylesheet. R4 requires the streak to be visible on all three variants in both themes, and the code now meets that: Styles/ZestButton.module.css:675-678 sets the solid band to #ffffff at peak 0.9, :680-682 and :706-708 switch dark-theme success to #064e3b, and :744-746 gives the split solid band peak 0.9. Recomputing the six solid combinations gives light standard 7.38, light success 3.34, light danger 4.14, dark standard 3.28, dark success 4.19 and dark danger 3.30, all >=3:1. The claim that the test only regex-matches is also wrong: __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:329-378 parses the colour/peak tokens, alpha-blends them over the theme background tokens in sRGB and asserts >=3:1 for every regular and split solid combination (it drops below 3 at peak 0.80). OS dark is covered because UI/ZestButton.tsx:241 resolves 'system' to the detected theme and :446 always applies force-light/force-dark. QA-1 was fixed in round 2 and REV-1 is a stale duplicate.

findings.description: A4 exists so the new prop can be found and read; the new guide links resolve in the git repo but 404 in the shipped package because `docs/` is not in `files`. Ship the guide inside `documentation/` (or `files`) or link to an always-available URL.
findings.evidence: `files` ships only `dist`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `documentation` (lines 28-33) - `docs/` is not published. The change adds links to `docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md` from README.md:145, documentation/api.md:220, documentation/configuration.md:136, documentation/examples.md:477 and documentation/features.md:264. In the published npm package those targets do not exist, so all five guide links are dead for consumers. (Existing `documentation/*.md` links only point inside `documentation/` or to the shipped `../README.md`, so this break is introduced by this change.)
findings.note: All five shipped pages now link the guide with the absolute public URL https://github.com/nyingimaina/jattac.libs.web.zest-button/blob/master/docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md (README.md:145, documentation/api.md:220, documentation/configuration.md:136, documentation/examples.md:477, documentation/features.md:264) and no relative `docs/features/...` link remains. The URL is valid for this repo: package.json:6-9 repository is git+https://github.com/nyingimaina/jattac.libs.web.zest-button.git, the origin remote is identical, and origin/master exists, so blob/master resolves in the public repo after merge even though `files` still publishes only dist/README/LICENSE/documentation. `npm pack --dry-run` confirms docs/ is still not in the tarball (32 files, no docs/), which is exactly why the absolute URL, not the relative path, is the correct target. The new A4 test (__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:505-521) asserts every shipped page contains that URL and none contains the unpublished relative docs/ link. Verification run: `npx jest --coverage=false` = 26 suites / 334 tests passed, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exits 0.

findings.description: R4 requires each style/variant/theme band to be distinguishable from its own background at >= 3:1 at its brightest point; solid success and danger in both themes (and dark standard) fall below 3:1 and no test would fail if the band were made even fainter.
findings.evidence: The solid band is currentColor (#ffffff on solid) at --zest-focus-sheen-peak: 0.65 (line 668 base 0.7, line 672 solid 0.65, keyframes lines 749-764). Blending that peak over the solid backgrounds defined at lines 84-92 (light) and 109-117 (dark) gives rgb(168,218,203) on #059669 = 2.43:1, rgb(243,179,179) on #dc2626 = 2.74:1, rgb(186,211,252) on #3b82f6 = 2.42:1, rgb(184,240,219) on #34d399 = 1.51:1 and rgb(249,190,190) on #ef4444 = 2.35:1. The only R4 colour test (__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:271-288) asserts token names, that every peak is < 1, and pins the 0.65 solid peak; it never computes contrast, so it passes with these ratios. The style-only matrix at lines 187-218 checks classes, not visibility.
findings.note: Solid bands now use #ffffff at --zest-focus-sheen-peak: 0.9 (Styles/ZestButton.module.css:675-678), with a #064e3b dark band for dark-theme success (lines 680-682); split equivalents at lines 700-707 and 744-745. The new test (__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:329) parses band colour, peak and the force-light/force-dark background tokens from the stylesheet, WCAG alpha-blends and asserts >=3:1 for all six solid combos on both regular and split. Independently recomputed at 0.9: light standard 7.38, light success 3.34, light danger 4.14, dark standard 3.28, dark success 4.19, dark danger 3.30; at 0.80 light success falls to 2.95 and dark standard to 2.92, so the test would fail if the band were made fainter. Full suite ran: 26 suites / 333 tests pass with --coverage=false. (The packed-library consumer smoke check still does not exist in this project, so it did not run.)

findings.description: R5's single-sweep iteration, leave-and-return restart, and long-label full-width edge cases are proven only by selector/class presence, not by an assertion that would fail if the split sweep repeated or failed to restart.
findings.evidence: The split assertion stops at the animation name (line 301); unlike the regular assertion at lines 120-122 it never checks '1 both', so the split rule could loop forever and still pass. The 'leaving the control and returning does [start a new sweep]' half of the R5 edge case is never exercised (lines 333-344 only focus main then chevron and count one .focusSheenSplit). The long-label edge case (lines 318-331) renders 'A very long main action label' but only asserts the menu is outside the wrapper/visible, never that one sweep spans the full width.

findings.description: The click-then-keyboard-focus sequence named in R2's edge cases has no test that drives that order; the guarantee rests on a CSS selector string assertion.
findings.evidence: The R2 test fires focus first and click second (lines 101-102), so it does not exercise the R2 edge case 'a mouse click followed by keyboard focus' in that order; the only proof that a mouse click plays nothing is the source regex for :focus-visible at lines 106-108.

findings.description: R3's aspect-ratio continuity and mid-sweep re-focus edge cases are only covered structurally (percentage sizing / one rule), not by a test of those states.
findings.evidence: The 'very small and very large' test only asserts two .focusSheen classes exist and one ::after rule exists (lines 173-183); it renders size sm/lg, never a wide-short or tall-narrow button, so R3's 'crosses the full button in one continuous sweep' on extreme aspect ratios is not asserted. The 'focusing again during a sweep' case (lines 111-124) blurs before re-focusing, so it does not re-trigger mid-sweep.

findings.description: The new public prop is not proven from the published entry point and the packed CJS/ESM import was not run. Informational under the project's missing packaging checks.
findings.evidence: No packed-library check exists (no scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs; attw/publint are not installed), and no test imports ZestButton or focusSheen through the package entry (UI/index.ts or dist); the new tests import ../UI/ZestButton directly.

findings.description: R4's 'every style distinguishable at >=3:1' acceptance is proven only for solid; outline/text/dashed bands over the page are unproven and text.success light computes below 3:1.
findings.evidence: Regular non-solid buttons take the base band colour currentColor at --zest-focus-sheen-peak: 0.7 (gradient line 660, peak line 668); split non-solid uses the variant border token at the same 0.7 peak (lines 709-722, 741). Alpha-blending over a light page: text.success light (--zest-color-success-bg #059669) at 0.7 over white gives rgb(80,182,150) = 2.49:1, and split sheenText.sheenSuccess light uses the same #059669 = 2.49:1, both below R4's stated 3:1. R4's only contrast test (__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:329) computes solid fills only; no test asserts a text-style band against the page, so the R4 edge case 'A text-style button with no fill behind it must still show a band against the page' has no test that would fail if the band were invisible there.

findings.description: Split-control leave-and-return replay is not proven.
findings.evidence: The R5 edge case 'Moving focus from the main segment to the chevron within one visit ...; leaving the control and returning does' is only half tested: __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:431 fires focus on the main button then the trigger and asserts one wrapper overlay, but no test blurs the whole split control and re-focuses to prove a new sweep starts on return. The only re-focus/replay test (R2, same file) covers a regular button, not a split control.

findings.description: Non-solid light-theme success bands are 2.49:1 against a white page, below R4's 3:1 acceptance, and no test covers non-solid contrast.
findings.evidence: The non-solid regular band falls back to `currentColor` at --zest-focus-sheen-peak: 0.7 (gradient line 660, peak line 668), and the non-solid split band uses the variant border token at the same 0.7 peak (`--zest-focus-sheen-color: var(--zest-color-success-border)` line 717, peak line 741). For light-theme success that token is #059669 (lines 13/87), so alpha-blending 0.7 over a white page gives rgb(80,182,150) = 2.49:1, below R4's required 3:1 at the band's brightest point. This affects outline.success, text.success and dashed.success in the light theme on both regular and split buttons (six combinations). The only contrast test (__tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:329-378) computes solid fills only, so nothing fails if these bands are too faint. R4's edge case 'A text-style button with no fill behind it must still show a band against the page' is therefore not met at the stated threshold for success in the light theme.

findings.description: Split-control leave-and-return replay is not proven by any test; only regular-button replay is covered.
findings.evidence: The only split-control focus test fires focus on the main button then the trigger (lines 436-437) and asserts a single .focusSheenSplit overlay; it never blurs the whole control and re-focuses to prove a fresh sweep on return. The only blur/re-focus replay test (lines 158-171) is for a regular button, not a split control. R5's edge case 'leaving the control and returning does [start a new sweep]' has no test that would fail if the split sweep failed to restart.

rulings.reason: REV-1 describes the pre-round-2 stylesheet. R4 requires the streak to be visible on all three variants in both themes, and the code now meets that: Styles/ZestButton.module.css:675-678 sets the solid band to #ffffff at peak 0.9, :680-682 and :706-708 switch dark-theme success to #064e3b, and :744-746 gives the split solid band peak 0.9. Recomputing the six solid combinations gives light standard 7.38, light success 3.34, light danger 4.14, dark standard 3.28, dark success 4.19 and dark danger 3.30, all >=3:1. The claim that the test only regex-matches is also wrong: __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx:329-378 parses the colour/peak tokens, alpha-blends them over the theme background tokens in sRGB and asserts >=3:1 for every regular and split solid combination (it drops below 3 at peak 0.80). OS dark is covered because UI/ZestButton.tsx:241 resolves 'system' to the detected theme and :446 always applies force-light/force-dark. QA-1 was fixed in round 2 and REV-1 is a stale duplicate.

acceptedAdditions.title: Turn the focus streak off for reduced motion
acceptedAdditions.why: People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a sweeping band.
acceptedAdditions.reason: A1: People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a fast sweeping band, and the existing streak is already switched off for them, so this follows an agreed accessibility setting rather than adding a new feature.; A2: The request already says the focus sweep should replace the chevron's one-time entrance streak on opted-in split buttons so two streaks do not collide, so this is the agreed behaviour and leaves every other button unchanged.
